_comment: CatBootstrap's three roles. Declared rather than left implicit in the diagram's lanes, which is where they lived until 2026-09-20 — a lane name is a string the audit cannot bind to anything, so `Bootstrapping agent` and `Person asking (judgement only)` appeared in the graph as roles nobody had defined. A role is the swimlane; an actor takes it on for the duration.
name: bootstrap

roles.title: Initiator
roles.description: An agent being requested to initialize a cat-harness with ONLY the knowledge bootstrap/README.md hands it. That constraint is the role, not a caveat on it: an Initiator has no MCP server, no harness, no work plan and no skills beyond those bootstrap carries, and a step that assumes any of those is a step an Initiator cannot perform. It stops being an Initiator the moment the harness is installed and it re-enters through that harness instead.
roles.persona: Knows nothing about this repository and cannot look anything up. Reads files, follows the processes bootstrap carries, and asks exactly one question when it must — `discussion` is how that asking is performed and what it must produce.

roles.title: Knowledge Graph Data Store
roles.description: A git repository, reached either through the git CLI or through a forge's API. It is where a declaration and its graph are READ from and where a new instance's declaration is WRITTEN to. It is `actedUpon`: it holds and serves, and takes no part in deciding what should happen — which is why it carries no skills and why naming one for it would be a lie about what it does.

roles.title: Requestor
roles.description: Wants to initialize — or bootstrap, or install, or load, or harness — a harness: bootstrap itself, or a derivative such as cat-harness, folio-assistant or smart-guidelines. Carries no skills deliberately: WHICH harness this repository should become is a judgement about intent, and no instruction body produces it. The Initiator may narrow the list from context; only the Requestor settles it.

roles.title: Logger
roles.description: A machine that accepts log messages and puts them somewhere a person can read. Like the Knowledge Graph Data Store it is `actedUpon` — it receives and records, takes no part in what happens next, and carries no skills, because the skill belongs to whoever is DOING the thing being logged. The Logger is not the author of a log line; it is where the line goes. That distinction is why `log-message` takes `actor` as a required input: the Logger cannot infer who acted, and a log that names the logger rather than the actor records nothing worth having.
